system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s update is a proposal, not an agreed or authorised position. In particular, neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period is cleared merely because it matches a possible fallback.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m. | 25% / AUD 6m starting position. | **Reject 20% for now** — it requires Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying this draft; none has been given. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Counter both thresholds and the excess-only mechanism** — the draft materially reduces recoverable claims. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | 18 months; limitations potentially extend to all Claims. | 24 months for general Warranty Claims, without spillover to other categories. | **Reject 18 months and the all-Claims wording** — the shorter period needs Amelia’s written approval and must not constrain separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Same cap and period as general warranties. | Separate 100% cap, at least six years, outside general thresholds and knowledge exclusions. | **Require a standalone regime** — ownership and capacity risk must not be diluted by general-claim limits. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out** — this protection is non-waivable under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Whole data room, registers and public records deemed disclosed. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranties. | **Delete blanket deemed disclosure** — availability of material is not a substitute for identifying the relevant exception fairly. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars matters known to Buyer or advisers, including discoverable material. | Delete blanket bar; any seller-knowledge qualifier must name persons and require reasonable enquiry, and cannot excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject clause 8.3 as drafted** — it transfers undisclosed and merely discoverable risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; written consent treated as sufficient on delivery. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions. | Effective consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied** before Completion. | **Keep this as a substantive completion condition** — Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. | **Reject unsecured post-Completion release** — an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia’s approval is required even to consider that fallback. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unstated. | Specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding for bonuses and triggered on-costs. | **Revise and verify the funds flow** — omission must not leave Buyer bearing an unpriced Completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 shown open, without independent verification. | Broader IP protection while preserving a documented SOW3 payment/assignment cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment and title evidence** — the open amount proves neither payment nor non-payment. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, notification duty or loss established. | Preserve logs, investigate scope and access, assess obligations, and provide updates. | **Require an investigation and reporting covenant** — do not assume either a confirmed breach or that the incident is immaterial. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate described as ordinary-course costs. | Assess timing, scope, accrual, avoidability and termination rights. | **Reserve treatment pending evidence** — do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from price. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations proposed across all Claims; tax and IP said to be settled. | Separate Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant and general Warranty regimes with no hidden override. | **Mark up every cross-reference and priority clause** — broad “all Claims” language could undo negotiated category protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 internal share register offered as evidence of 100% title. | Independent ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. | **Require independent verification** — the supplied register identifies a source, not conclusive proof of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says both are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms open for express negotiation; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Reject the asserted settlement** — no buyer authority or completed agreement establishes it. |
=== END ADVICE ===
